EME 200: This introductory course provides a comprehensive overview of subsurface energy resources and their engineering principles.
EME 210: Data Analytics for Energy Systems merges introductory statistics with coding through simulation-based inference.
EME 301: Treatment of classical thermodynamics targeted to the needs of students in the Department of Energy and Mineral Engineering.
EME 303: Treatment of fluid mechanics targeted to the needs of students in the Department of EME.
EME 407: Electrochemical concepts in energy storage devices, cell construction and materials involved in batteries and capacitors, electrochemical testing methods and applications.
EME 428: Large-scale deployment of negative emissions technologies (NET's) will be critical to minimize the worst impacts of climate change.
EME 432: Analysis, formulation, implementation, and impacts of energy-related policies, regulations, and initiatives.
EME 444: Global Energy Enterprise provides in-depth insight into the role that public and private nonmarket actors and actions play in contemporary energy markets through a variety of artifacts and case studies.
EME 450: Energy Crisis Leadership accelerates developing leadership skills, self-awareness, confidence, and character through evidence-based and experiential learning activities.
EME 460: The course covers engineering evaluation of geo-resources, present value and rate of return analysis, mineral property and reserve estimation, and cost estimation and engineering economy concepts applied to geo-resources including energy and minerals.
EME 466: EME 466 provides the culminating experience for Energy and Sustainability Policy majors through an individualized inquiry-based capstone project in which students tackle the wicked problems of sustainability they see and experience in their own communities.
